title: Meat without the animal
text:
Meat grown from animal cells in a laboratory, rather than taken from a slaughtered animal, was until recently regarded as [[1]] stuff of science fiction. Today, a handful of companies are selling it, although only in small quantities and at prices [[2]] put it out of reach of most shoppers.

The process begins [[3]] a small sample of cells taken from a living animal. These are then fed nutrients in large steel tanks until they multiply. In theory, it would take only a few cells to produce [[4]] meat to feed a whole town. Supporters claim that, if the technology were adopted on a large scale, it [[5]] dramatically reduce the land and water used for farming.

No sooner [[6]] the first products gone on sale than critics began to raise objections. Some question whether the energy needed to run the tanks would cancel [[7]] the environmental benefits. Others doubt that consumers will ever trust food made in a factory. Whatever the outcome, few experts expect lab-grown meat to replace farming altogether; at most, [[8]] will become one option among many.

explanation.en: 'The stuff of science fiction' (or 'of dreams', 'of legend') is a fixed pattern meaning 'something that belongs in science fiction'. It always takes the definite article.
explanation.cs: Spojení 'the stuff of science fiction' = něco jako z vědeckofantastického románu. Používá se se členem 'the'.

explanation.en: A defining relative clause describes the prices: 'prices that put it out of reach'. There is no comma, so both 'that' and 'which' are accepted.
explanation.cs: Vztažná věta bez čárky určuje, o jaké ceny jde, proto 'that' i 'which'. 'What' tu nejde, protože už máme podstatné jméno 'prices'.

explanation.en: 'Begin with something' names the first stage of a process: 'The process begins with a small sample'. 'By' would need an -ing form ('begins by taking').
explanation.cs: 'Begin with sth' = začínat něčím. 'Begin by' se používá s -ing (begins by taking cells), ne s podstatným jménem.

explanation.en: 'Enough meat to feed a whole town' uses the pattern enough + noun + 'to' infinitive. 'Sufficient' works in the same position and is also accepted; 'much' would need 'so much ... that' or 'too'.
explanation.cs: Vazba enough + podstatné jméno + to + infinitiv = dost masa na to, aby. Uznává se i formálnější 'sufficient'.

explanation.en: 'If the technology were adopted' is a second conditional, so the main clause needs a past modal: 'it could (would, might) dramatically reduce'. 'Will' does not match the unreal 'were' in the if-clause.
explanation.cs: Druhý kondicionál (if ... were adopted) chce v hlavní větě would, could nebo might. 'Will' patří k prvnímu kondicionálu a s 'were' nejde dohromady.

explanation.en: 'No sooner' at the start of a sentence causes inversion with the past perfect: 'No sooner had the first products gone on sale than critics began'. The participle 'gone' and the later 'than' are the clues.
explanation.cs: Po 'No sooner' na začátku věty následuje inverze s předminulým časem: had + podmět + příčestí. Nápovědou je 'gone' a dále 'than'.

explanation.en: 'Cancel out' means to balance something so that it has no effect: the energy used might cancel out the benefits. 'Cancel off' or 'cancel down' are not used with this meaning.
explanation.cs: 'Cancel out' = vyrušit, vynulovat účinek něčeho. Spotřeba energie by mohla smazat ekologický přínos.

explanation.en: The clause needs a subject that refers back to 'lab-grown meat': 'at most, it will become one option'. 'This' is also accepted; 'they' does not agree with the uncountable 'meat'.
explanation.cs: Věta potřebuje podmět odkazující na 'lab-grown meat'. 'Meat' je nepočitatelné, proto 'it' (případně 'this'), ne 'they'.
